rationale: parse5 is a WHATWG HTML Living Standard-compliant HTML parser/serializer toolkit for Node.js. It provides the foundational HTML parsing layer used by major projects (jsdom, Angular, Lit, Cheerio, rehype). The monorepo contains 7 packages: core parse5 (parser + serializer + tree adapters), SAX streaming parser, parser stream with scripting support, plain-text conversion stream, HTML rewriting stream, and htmlparser2 tree adapter. Total ~10,800 lines of TypeScript source across 41 source files. Comprehensive test suite including html5lib tree-construction tests and parser feedback tests. However, parse5 does NOT directly implement any of the 8 pipeline concerns (jsonld-extraction, browser-automation, script-generation, self-healing, stealth, queue, fuzzy-matching, fulltext-search). It is a low-level building block that a scraping pipeline would depend on for HTML parsing, but it does not perform extraction, scheduling, stealth, or search indexing itself. Tier B reflects high architectural depth (full spec compliance with proper tokenizer, insertion modes, formatting element list, open element stack, tree adapter abstraction, streaming parsers) and production-grade maturity, but indirect relevance to the specific pipeline concerns.
limitations: Does not implement any of the 8 pipeline concerns directly — it is a foundational HTML parser, not a scraping framework
No browser automation, stealth, or anti-bot features
